discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 230619
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
119 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably cold today with highs in the 40s.

- There is a 20% chance of rain showers after sunset, mainly 
  for northern areas. Snow may briefly mix in late. 

- 60% to 80% chance of rain on Thanksgiving. Snowflakes may mix
  in later Thursday night. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 116 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

Cold northwest flow has enveloped the area and has brewed up a batch 
of lake effect cloud streets. Seasonably crisp early this morning 
with temperatures currently in the 40s, headed toward the 30s as 
cold air advection persists. Upstream, a shortwave is noted over the 
arrowhead of MN. This feature drops south through the day and by 
sunset this secondary push of cold air brings scattered rain and 
snow showers mainly along and north the Toll Road; lower confidence 
south of there. Rain will be primary precipitation type early in the 
evening, but as the hours tick on beyond sunset, snow will be more 
likely to mix in. This shortwaves moves quickly such that residence 
time of precipitation will generally be brief; moisture profiles are 
shallow as well. Dry conditions resume soon after midnight as high 
pressure undercuts precipitation. 

Dry for Tuesday and Wednesday with seasonably cold conditions as high 
pressure moves over the Great Lakes. Meanwhile, to the west, a deep 
trough encases the central US with a pair of 500-mb lows noted. 
These lows move over Midwest Wednesday night through Thursday. Sharp 
warm air advection on the eastern flank of the interior-most low 
favors primarily rain for our area Thursday. The magnitude of any 
cold air is currently locked up elsewhere. However, as the low 
matures over the Northeast US, cold air advection behind this low 
improves somewhat to permit some snow Thursday night into Friday. 
This is highly uncertain given the modest magnitude of cold air and 
our sensitive location on the western edge of this low. This has 
certainly been a quick ramp-up in POPs, now topping 60-80% 
(primarily rain) Wednesday night through at least Friday morning. 
Don't let social media fool you; this does not appear to be a 
blockbuster storm locally by any stretch. 

Troughing continues for the remainder of the holiday weekend keeping 
temperatures seasonably cool and we could see one or more shortwaves 
breeze by. Our seasonal whiplash returns next week as a trough out 
west buckles the downstream jet, sending our high temperatures back 
toward 50 degrees by the debut of December. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1222 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

The Pacific jet stream residing across the area exists at the 
base of a mid level trough through the Lower Great Lakes. This 
pushes a few vigorous vort maxes through the area in this TAF 
period. The first of these vort maxes pushes through this 
morning and this is the first cold punch into the area and it is
enough to keep the winds excited to around 10 kts with some 
gusts around 20 kts possible at times through the period. 
Another vort max pushes through today and that may be enough to 
set off some lake enhanced rain/snow showers. Given the dry air 
and relative proximity away from Lake MI, will keep these out of
the TAFs for now. Aside from the first few hours of these TAFs,
aviation guidance continues to indicate that any clouds will be
higher than MVFR criteria and so will continue with VFR in 
these TAFs. Although, it is possible that there is a tempo for 
high MVFR in a future iteration of SBN's TAFs mainly for the 15 
to 22z time period where cold air overtops the relative warm air
at the surface and lingering lake enhancement encourages 
saturation.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 AM EST Tuesday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Roller

spc.text:
SPC AC 230547

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1147 PM CST Sun Nov 22 2026

   Valid 231200Z - 241200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely today.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deep mid/upper-level trough will move from the Great Lakes and
   Upper Midwest region towards the Northeast later today. This system
   will reinforce a cold front that will continue moving southeastward
   across parts of the Southeast and Gulf Coast. Storms may be ongoing
   at the start of the period across parts of south TX, before the
   front pushes offshore in this region. Diurnal storm development will
   be possible near the front across the central Gulf Coast,
   potentially aided by a weak midlevel southern-stream shortwave
   trough. Severe potential will be limited by generally weak
   instability and very modest deep-layer flow/shear.  

   Elsewhere, a mid/upper-level shortwave trough moving across the
   Southwest may aid in the development of weak elevated convection
   across parts of southern NM and Far West TX tonight. Buoyancy will
   remain quite meager, but sporadic lightning flashes could accompany
   this activity into early Tuesday morning.

   ..Dean/Jirak.. 11/23/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 230658

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1258 AM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms are possible over parts of western/southern
   Texas, the Gulf Coast, Florida, and the West Coast Tuesday. Severe
   storms are not expected.

   ...Synopsis...
   A broad upper trough over the High Plains is forecast to intensify
   as it moves southeastward across the Rio Grande and toward the Gulf
   Coast Tuesday. A second upper trough will approach the West Coast,
   gradually weakening as it moves onshore. Offshore flow across the
   Gulf and parts of the East Coast will continue as surface high
   pressure shifts eastward ahead of the upper trough. To the south of
   the high, a surface cyclone is expected to develop across the
   northern Gulf late Tuesday into early Wednesday.

   ...Rio Grande Valley to the Gulf Coast...
   Given the strong offshore flow in the wake of a prior cold front,
   substantial boundary-layer moisture is expected to remain mostly
   offshore. Cool mid-level temperatures beneath the intensifying upper
   trough may support weak buoyancy sufficient for isolated lightning
   flashes Tuesday afternoon into Tuesday night. Additional elevated
   storms are possible along the northern Gulf Coast ahead of the
   deepening surface low. Given very weak buoyancy, none of these
   storms are expected to be severe.

   ...West Coast...
   Additional sporadic lightning flashes are possible ahead of the West
   Coast trough as a strong cold front is forecast to move ashore. A
   shallow convective line is expected to approach the northern CA
   during the afternoon with weak buoyancy. Additional more cellular
   storms may liner off the coast of WA/OR through Tuesday night.
   Occasional lightning and a few stronger wind gusts are possible
   given the stronger flow within the lowest 3-4 km, but severe storms
   are not expected.

   ...South FL and the Keys...
   Late in the forecast period, an embedded shortwave trough ahead of
   the upper trough will begin to overspread the FL Straits and
   southern Peninsula. Some model solutions show a cluster of
   thunderstorms developing near the Keys spreading northeastward by
   12z Wednesday. Mid-level lapse rates and vertical shear do not
   appear overly robust, and considerable model spread exists. However,
   sporadic damaging gusts or a waterspout are possible, but confidence
   in more organized/widespread severe potential is low.

   ..Lyons.. 11/23/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 230829

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0229 AM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTH FLORIDA AND THE KEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over parts of South
   Florida Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An initially loosely organized upper trough, with multiple embedded
   mid-level cyclones will gradually coalesce as it moves across the MS
   Valley and northern Gulf Wednesday. The southernmost of the
   mid-level cyclones should amplify as it approaches FL, helping to
   deepen a surface low across the FL Straits before it moves into the
   western Atlantic. Thunderstorms are likely across much of the Gulf
   and FL, where isolated strong to severe storms are possible.

   ...South FL...
   A lead shortwave trough will move over the Keys and South FL early
   Wednesday, ahead of the unusually deep upper low moving across the
   northern Gulf. Mid-level southwesterly flow is expected to increase
   as the Gulf surface low approaches. Typical upper 70s F surface
   dewpoints should allow for tall/skinny buoyancy thermodynamic
   profiles to develop. Scattered thunderstorms, are expected near the
   Keys and may move across south FL through the first half of the day
   near the surface low. The strengthening flow aloft could support
   some organization into linear clusters or supercells with a threat
   for damaging winds and perhaps a tornado. By later in the day, the
   low will move across the Peninsula toward the Atlantic Coast, with a
   strengthening cold front trailing behind it. This should veer
   low-level flow and end the convective threat Wednesday evening.

   ...Coastal Carolinas...
   As the low intensifies and quickly lifts northeastward along the
   Atlantic Coast, some model guidance shows a warm front moving inland
   across the eastern Carolinas late Wednesday night into early
   Thursday morning. Model soundings show a very moist air mass within
   a strengthening wind field. Buoyancy appears rather limited, with
   the nocturnal timing and poor lapse rates. However, some
   thunderstorm potential is evident given the strong synoptic ascent
   and low-level moisture advection. Severe potential is much less
   certain, as model spread remains quite large regarding the frontal
   positions and available warm sector inland.

   ..Lyons.. 11/23/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
